title: Global nomads
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Have you ever felt more at home with people who have lived in many places?

Jose asked: why is the first friend he makes a man like this? A student said: because he's well traveled and culturally diverse, and he complements him. Jose said: there is a very interesting phenomenon with children who have grown up in different cultures. They are called global nomads.

A global nomad is somebody who has lived in more than two countries in their life, he said. They develop an identity around having moved. A student said it makes you less of a nationalist and more of a globalist. Jose said: you're more culturally suspended, because your identity is not attached to a specific country or culture.

That has a big impact on your relationships with people who have grown up in the same small town their whole life, Jose said. A monocultural person has had the same friends their whole life, so their adaptation to change is generally slower. There is natural conflict, because the multicultural person sees things on a more global level.

A specific example, he said: a multicultural person discloses personal information without considering it a risk. The monocultural person thinks: why is this person telling me their whole life story in five minutes?

As Jose retells it, the author meets the person closest to his own reality: a mix of countries, thinking multiculturally and in the big picture. They start to play games that simulate reality, and a student said their goals outside the game are very different from a person of one culture: they are thinking at a much higher level.
Where have you lived, and who understands that?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the places you have lived or worked in.
Write how that shaped how you open up to people.
Write a time you and a person from a single place misread each other.
Write one thing a multicultural person could teach you.
Write one thing you could teach a monocultural friend.

check.q: What did Jose call someone who has lived in more than two countries?
What did Jose say a monocultural person's adaptation to change is generally?
What did Jose say a multicultural person does with personal information?
choices: Discloses it without considering it a risk

recap: Notice how where you have lived shapes how you connect.
